Subject: FinLytics — post-demo recap, model recommendations & quantization plan

Hey Sarah — great meeting today, thanks for walking through the ingestion + redaction constraints and the latency target (p95 <= 450ms) for your paid product flows. Quick recap and recommended next steps: 

1) Primary goals we heard
- Low-latency semantic search and short-form generation for summaries (customer-facing)
- Strict auditability: no persistent PII leakage, request-level logging
- Quality floor: hallucination rate < 2% on our gold eval set

2) Recommended models to evaluate (small-to-large sweep)
- Mistral-7B-instruct (fastest on cost-sensitive endpoints)
- LLaMA-2-13B-chat (good balance of quality + cost)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (high-quality fallback for critical flows)

3) Quantization/throughput guidance we suggest for your PoC
- AWQ (4-bit) for latency-sensitive endpoints where a small, controlled regression is acceptable; expect ~2.0–2.8x token/sec improvements vs 16-bit depending on sequence length.
- GPTQ (4-bit) gives similar throughput gains but is more model-dependent; some model families show larger quality variance after GPTQ.
- FP8 (mixed or hybrid FP8 kernels) keeps quality closest to FP16 while still improving throughput — good compromise for high-fidelity outputs.

4) Proposed PoC plan (mutual action items)
- Redwood: run a 48-hour eval using your provided prompt set and gold labels across the three models above with AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 profiles and share aggregated benchmarks + per-prompt regression notes. (See attached: finlytics_prompt_samples.json)
- FinLytics: share a sanitized dev slice (1k queries) marked for hallucination and precision checks.
- Align on success criteria (we recommend hallucination <2%, ROUGE/L other thresholds) and then run a 2-week dedicated pilot on Dedicated capacity if results look good.

Attachments: finlytics_prompt_samples.json (sample prompts), mutual_action_plan.docx (initial timeline)

I'll kick off the benchmark run once you confirm the sanitized dataset. Happy to jump on a short follow-up to walk through the quantization tradeoffs live.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah — quick technical answers to your questions (short bullets + pointer to attached benchmark CSV):

- AWQ vs GPTQ failure modes:
  * AWQ (our measurements across LLaMA/Falcon families): typical regressions are subtle token-choice differences (conservative wording shifts) and occasional numeric rounding issues when prompts require precise table-to-text extraction. We saw ~0.8–1.8% absolute increase in hallucination on targeted numeric QA tests for some models after AWQ 4-bit.
  * GPTQ: larger variance across model families — some LLaMA-derived variants showed up to 3.5% regression on the same numeric QA set after GPTQ-4. GPTQ can be brittle if the quantization calibration step is not tuned per-model.

- FP8 tradeoffs:
  * FP8 (hybrid kernels): maintains quality within ~0.1–0.4% of FP16 on our gold sets while delivering ~1.4–1.9x throughput improvements. Cost delta estimate: FP8 runs typically cost ~20–35% more than AWQ-4 (depending on instance type and effective batching) but often cheaper than full FP16.

- Latency and KV-cache scenarios:
  * Benchmarks will include token-level p50/p95/p99, and separate warm vs cold KV-cache runs for both chat (stateful) and stateless generation. We'll also include per-token compute vs batching overhead breakdown. See attached: benchmark_results_v1.csv (summary).

Recommendation for PoC setup:
- Start with Mistral-7B + AWQ-4 for your real-time low-latency endpoint. Use LLaMA-2-13B with FP8 as the high-fidelity path for billing-sensitive or human-reviewed outputs. Only route to Falcon-40B for the small % of requests flagged for high-criticality outputs.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood: run the 48-hour full-sweep using your 1k slice when you share it (we'll post results to the Drive link and a short slide deck).
- FinLytics: share sanitized dataset by EOD Tue (18th) and a brief list of priority prompts that must pass with no hallucination.

Thanks — attached is the CSV export from our internal run. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech session if you'd like a walkthrough of the per-prompt diffs.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
